You return to the committee chapter and read through its examples of stalled petitions, provisional agreements, and decisions quietly reshaped before reaching the full Council.

By the final pages, one point has become difficult to miss: a seat holder’s public speech may matter, but so do the people choosing an agenda, assigning a committee, or deciding an issue can wait another season.

Across the library, Caelindra closes her protocol text with a restrained thump and leaves by the main door. Professor Stone continues working beneath the spiral stair, his blue pencil moving steadily through the ledger.

You finish the chapter beneath the library lamp, then rest your hand on the book’s worn blue cover.
